hints: Notice the nuclide notation $^{37}_{17}Cl$: the lower number 17 is the proton number $Z$ and the upper number 37 is the nucleon number $A$, so find the neutron number $N = A - Z$.
Recall the quark content of each nucleon: a proton is $uud$ with 2 up and 1 down, while a neutron is $udd$ with 1 up and 2 down.
Multiply 17 protons and 20 neutrons by their up and down content and add the two contributions to compare the totals 54 and 57.
walkthrough: Read $^{37}_{17}Cl$: proton number $Z = 17$, so there are 17 protons. Nucleon number $A = 37$, so neutron number $N = A - Z = 37 - 17 = 20$.
State the quark model: proton $= uud$, so each proton contributes 2 up quarks and 1 down quark. Neutron $= udd$, so each neutron contributes 1 up quark and 2 down quarks.
Calculate total up quarks: from protons $17 \times 2 = 34$ plus from neutrons $20 \times 1 = 20$, so $34 + 20 = 54$.
Calculate total down quarks: from protons $17 \times 1 = 17$ plus from neutrons $20 \times 2 = 40$, so $17 + 40 = 57$.
The nucleus therefore contains 54 up quarks and 57 down quarks. This is option B.
